currentContext.business: The Company imports, manufactures and processes high-quality natural stone — premium and exclusive Indian and imported marbles and granites — from its facility at Abu Road, Rajasthan, which management describes as one of the most technologically advanced in the sector. It supplies a wide range of textures, colours and finishes to luxury residential projects, commercial establishments, hospitality infrastructure and high-end interior applications, selling through long-standing relationships with niche clients, architects, interior designers and developers. The Company is also building an online and e-commerce presence via its website to widen reach for niche products.

currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no capex project, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up plan. Expansion is described only in market and product terms: the Company says it has identified several new opportunities for growth including expansion of product offerings and introduction of a wider range of colours, and that it continues to widen its client base both geographically and numerically, hoping to expand further with the introduction of an e-commerce facility on its website in the coming years. Its manufacturing and processing facility at Abu Road, Rajasthan is described as remaining one of the most technologically advanced in the sector, but no capacity figure, expansion or new line is mentioned. The Company confirms it has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company, so no inorganic capacity or geography addition is disclosed. On technology, the Company states it undertakes studies from time to time for process improvement and plant design development, with no separate research and development department and no quantifiable R&D spend.

risks.note: Explicitly listed by management as a business risk. The Company's core business is importing premium marble and natural stone, so landed cost and margin move with the rupee; the cautionary statement also names foreign exchange fluctuations among factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.

risks.risk: Volatility in freight and logistics costs and global supply-chain disruption
risks.note: Named as a business risk and again in the industry-structure section: the marble industry saw fluctuations in freight costs and disruptions in global supply chains from geopolitical developments, which directly affect an import-led model shipping stone from 30 countries.

risks.risk: Changes in import regulations and duties
risks.note: Listed as a business risk. Since the product range is dominated by imported Italian and exotic marble and granite, any change in import duty or regulation hits cost structure and competitiveness.

risks.risk: Slowdown in the real estate and infrastructure sectors
risks.note: Listed as a business risk. Demand is concentrated in luxury residential, commercial, hospitality and premium interiors, so a downturn in real estate or infrastructure spending directly reduces offtake; management notes external factors already affected short-term growth in FY2025-26 after a prior year of strong residential and commercial demand.

risks.risk: Increasing competition and price pressure from artificial stone alternatives
risks.note: Flagged both as a business risk and under Opportunities and Threats — competition plus substitution by engineered/artificial stone creates price pressure, which the Company says it is addressing through product mix, supply-chain resilience and customer engagement.
Named under Opportunities and Threats as a persisting challenge alongside competition and price pressure, squeezing realisations in a premium but price-sensitive category.

The Company's investment portfolio was impacted by market volatility from geopolitical developments and it recognised a diminution in the value of certain investments during the year. This makes reported earnings sensitive to non-operating asset values; management calls the decline temporary and says it follows a conservative and prudent approach to investment decisions.

risks.risk: Geopolitical tensions, war situations and global macro uncertainty
risks.note: Recurs across the MD's communique, MD&A and the cautionary statement — it is the stated transmission channel into supply chains, commodity and currency movements, investor sentiment and the Company's own asset valuations.
